statements.quote: These policies have to be simultaneous, or I cannot support them.
statements.claim: Despite marking no in the short-answer section, supports overdose-prevention centers only together with other policies intended to keep neighborhood residents safe. He acknowledges their public-health value; a blanket anti-harm-reduction label would misstate the explanation.

statements.quote: I would support the opening of an Overdose Prevention Center
statements.claim: Does not support a center in District7, but would support one elsewhere if residents' quality of life is not negatively affected. Her blank checkbox does not mean no substantive position.

statements.answer_context: Will you publicly support decreasing public schools reliance on police and school resource officers and instead work with the school district to prioritize life-affirming programs and staffing in schools including by hiring multiple counselors and nurses? YES [X] NO [ ]
statements.claim: Marks support for decreasing school reliance on police and school resource officers while prioritizing other support staff.

statements.answer_context: I believe we must increase the numbers of counselors, nurses and life affirming, trauma informed programs. I don’t believe that the current number of school resource officers is making our schools less safe. I believe we need both.
statements.claim: Marks no to reducing reliance on school police, then explains that she supports both school officers and more counselors, nurses and trauma-informed programs.

statements.answer_context: Do you commit to supporting a city-wide ban on the use of natural gas or other fossil fuels in new buildings (with very limited exceptions), similar to the bans recently enacted in NYC, Washington DC and other cities? YES [X] NO [ ]
statements.claim: Commits to the proposed citywide fossil-fuel ban for new buildings with limited exceptions.

statements.answer_context: Do you commit to supporting a city-wide ban on the use of natural gas or other fossil fuels in new buildings (with very limited exceptions), similar to the bans recently enacted in NYC, Washington DC and other cities? YES [ ] NO [X]
statements.claim: Does not commit to that ban at this time; her explanation supports reducing fossil-fuel reliance and an eventual ban. It is not categorical opposition to decarbonization.

statements.claim: Supports funding the public-bank initiative named in the questionnaire. This does not independently certify the institution's operating or licensing status.

statements.claim: Leaves the cap checkbox blank and says she is open to studying rent controls and other affordability measures. The response is unresolved, not explicit rejection.

statements.quote: the development of new units of affordable housing
statements.claim: Prioritizes production of more affordable homes, with stronger inclusionary zoning, land-bank use for affordable housing and land trusts, and community-benefit standards.

statements.quote: increase the supply of public and affordable housing construction
statements.claim: Supports expanding public and affordable housing alongside homeownership assistance and efforts to address poverty.

statements.quote: working-class community leaders to have real influence
statements.claim: Would use the council seat to build community power over priorities, policy design and resource allocation.

statements.quote: how to address the hundred or so constituent calls
statements.claim: Emphasizes experience serving residents and navigating government constraints. The claimed service volume is attributed, not independently measured.

comparisons.analysis: Celin conditions support on simultaneous neighborhood-safety measures; Lozada rules out her district but supports a center elsewhere under quality-of-life conditions. Their explanations matter more than treating a no mark or blank checkbox as blanket opposition.

Celin supports decreasing reliance on school police in favor of other staff; Lozada opposes that shift and explicitly wants both officers and additional counselors/nurses. She is not coded as opposing student support services.

Celin commits to the proposed fossil-fuel ban for new buildings; Lozada declines the current proposal while supporting an eventual ban. The disagreement concerns current commitment and timing, not whether climate change is real.
Both support funding the same public-bank initiative named in the question. Their other differences do not erase this concrete agreement.
Celin supports the specified ceiling; Lozada is open to exploration without committing to it. Uncertainty is not converted into an opposing stance.

Both support more affordable housing production, with Celin emphasizing public land, inclusionary requirements and community control and Lozada also emphasizing homeownership and economic opportunity.

Celin foregrounds community power over policy and budgets; Lozada foregrounds constituent service and experienced navigation of government. Both describe engagement with residents rather than mutually exclusive goals.
